source.title: Specialization after Generalization: Towards Understanding Test-Time Training in Foundation Models
source.authors: Jonas Hübotter; Patrik Wolf; A. Shevchenko; Dennis Jüni; Andreas Krause; Gil Kur

page_placements.theme: Sparse local supports and task-dependent direction decompositions

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses the linear representation hypothesis and superimposed concepts as a framework for explaining test-time training, but does not test any of the listed claim versions. Its SAE experiments measure local concept support and neighborhood geometry in ImageNet embeddings, not the listed toy-model or LLM claims.
record.gate_note: The paper assumes sparse concept representations and superposition in its theoretical account. It reports SAE-based measurements on ImageNet embeddings, including local neighborhood geometry and the number of concepts selected by an adaptive mask. These findings are related to the claim's subject but do not test any listed version: the experiments are not toy-model superposition tests, LLM feature analyses, or tests of feature dimensionality or canonicality.
record.test_reason: The paper assumes the linear representation hypothesis and superposition of concepts (citing Elhage et al., 2022) as a framework for explaining test-time training. Its SAE experiments on ImageNet CLIP embeddings and MNIST measure local neighborhood geometry, concept support of neighborhoods, and agreement between TTT classifiers. None of these measures whether features are superposed in toy models, why neurons are polysemantic, whether LLMs spread features across neurons, whether SAE features are canonical, or feature dimensionality. The scaling results are task performance, and the 'fewer concepts superimposed at larger size' explanation is a hypothesis, not a measurement. The theory (Prop. 9) models superposition as random projection by construction.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors argue that foundation models are globally underparameterized. Under the LRH with superimposed concepts, TTT specializes capacity to locally relevant concepts and achieves lower in-distribution error than global training. SAE analyses suggest neighborhoods are supported by few concepts and that TTT implicitly favors sparse concept-space solutions. Scaling studies show TTT gains shrink as models grow.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops a test-time-training account using an assumed linear representation hypothesis and SAE analyses; it does not reproduce the toy-network methods or measurements from the original superposition work.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported ImageNet neighborhood-size sweep finds an optimal size reflecting a tradeoff between locality and diversity; the SAE mask sparsity depends on the stated mask penalty.

fits_no_version.finding: For neighborhoods of ImageNet CLIP embeddings, an adaptive mask keeps ~40 of ~180 active SAE concepts (λ=0.2) with TTT accuracy on par with dense reconstructions (72.64 vs 72.56). MNIST gives a similar result (mask ~24.5 of ~144.5 union concepts).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local neighborhoods in vision embeddings can be supported by a small adaptive subset of SAE concepts.

fits_no_version.finding: Concept-space cosine similarity distributions are nearly identical whether neighbors are selected in Ψ, Ψ̂ or Φ̂ space (figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A top-k SAE on CLIP embeddings approximately preserves local neighborhood geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: TTT in dense reconstruction space and in masked concept space agree on ~89% of predictions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: TTT in a dense feature space implicitly behaves like a sparse concept-space solution.

record.problems: The paper's theoretical account assumes the linear representation hypothesis and sparse concept structure. Its empirical SAE evidence is from ImageNet CLIP embeddings and MNIST rather than LLM activations; the reported neighborhood-similarity values are figure-only, and the text gives no numeric values for them.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported test-time-training scaling, dataset-size, and language-model results were left out because they measure task performance rather than the representation properties named in the claim. The non-adaptive-mask accuracy is also not separately included because it is an auxiliary comparison rather than a direct measurement of the claim's representation properties.

untested.parts: No toy-model experiment on superposition geometry or the sparsity transition. The random-projection construction in App. C.3 is assumed, not trained.
Neuron polysemanticity and importance-based capacity allocation are not measured.
No LLM activation or SAE analysis. The SAEs are on CLIP image embeddings and MNIST, and the LLM results are only bits-per-byte.
SAE features' completeness, stability and canonicality are not tested.

record.verdict_notes: Superposition here is a modeling assumption. The model-size explanation ('fewer concepts superimposed') is stated as a hypothesis without a representational measurement. The SAE training details (ghost gradients, 4% dead features) are tooling. The record omits the MNIST SAE numbers in App. F.2 but notes they are out of scope; they bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network experiment testing overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
Does not test neuron polysemanticity or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared capacity.
Does not study polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
The SAE experiments use ImageNet CLIP embeddings and MNIST, not LLM activations; the language-model experiments assess test-time training performance rather than feature distribution or SAE recovery.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.

relation.reason: The introduction and Section 5 assume a sparse concept space represented in a lower-dimensional feature space; the theory analyzes TTT under that framework.

tranche.reason: The study uses assumed superimposed concept representations to explain TTT; the listed results measure adaptive mask sparsity and classifier performance, without testing a superposition claim version.

source_check.notes: These rows describe the study's own method and comparator, not measurements of superposition. ImageNet results use SAE reconstructions; the approximately 40-concept mask depends on λ=0.2.
